question: Why is WebRTC preferred over WebSockets for voice AI transport?
options: WebRTC is easier to implement than WebSockets
WebRTC supports higher audio bitrates than WebSockets
WebRTC uses UDP, avoiding head-of-line blocking that causes audio stalls
explanation: WebRTC uses UDP via RTP, so each packet is independent. If one packet is lost, subsequent packets still arrive immediately. WebSockets use TCP, where a single lost packet stalls the entire stream (head-of-line blocking), causing 50-200ms delays that are devastating for conversational voice AI. WebRTC is not necessarily easier to implement, and WebSockets do support persistent connections.

question: In the voice AI latency budget, why is transport latency considered 'pure waste'?
options: Because transport only affects the server-to-user direction, not user-to-server
Because transport latency can be eliminated entirely with better hardware
Because unlike STT/LLM/TTS processing, transport produces nothing — it is dead time where bytes sit in buffers
Because transport is the most expensive part of the pipeline
explanation: Model processing stages (STT, LLM, TTS) produce useful output — transcriptions, generated text, synthesized audio. Transport latency produces nothing; it is simply time spent moving bytes between locations. Additionally, transport appears twice in the pipeline (user-to-server and server-to-user), so every millisecond of transport overhead is paid twice.
